cards.task: Stand directly above the yellow pyramid, facing it, and step forward to turn it into a purple star, then pick up the purple star to turn it into a blue pyramid, then stand so that the blue pyramid is one tile to your right on the map.

wrong.why: Turns in place for the whole episode, so the goal never fires.
Makes the purple star and the blue pyramid but never stands with the blue pyramid on its right (the scripted policy with the goal ignored).

cards.notes: XLand suite, the ARM-FM paper's Figure 9 task X1: ruleset 197 of xminigrid's medium-1m benchmark. The task text is reconstructed: the paper names the ruleset, not its text; experiments/benchmark/scripts/render_xland.py renders it from the ruleset. Each step's event is the tile it makes; also_ok takes the holding rule's pickup event, true on the same step as blue_pyramid_made. The order is forced by the rules and still stated, so it stays in. train: false keeps the card out of the 60-card set.

cards.task: Stand directly above the green pyramid, facing it, and step forward to turn it into a brown pyramid, then stand directly above the brown pyramid, facing it, and step forward to turn it into a blue ball, then step forward with the blue ball next to you.

wrong.why: Turns in place for the whole episode, so the goal never fires.
Makes the brown pyramid and stops there: the forward that makes the blue ball would also fire the goal, so the scripted policy with the goal ignored never takes it.

cards.task: Pick up the blue key and put it down next to the purple ball to make an orange star, then pick up the orange star.

wrong.why: Turns in place for the whole episode, so the goal never fires.
Makes the orange star but never picks it up (the scripted policy with the goal ignored).
Carries the purple ball to the blue key instead of the key to the ball: the orange star is made and picked up, but the blue key is never picked up first.

cards.notes: XLand suite, the ARM-FM paper's Figure 10 task A (a training task). The ruleset is rebuilt by hand from the figure, whose rules are only partly visible, and the task text is reconstructed from it by experiments/benchmark/scripts/render_xland.py. Picking up the key and putting it down to make the star is a compound step: the star needs the put-down, so the order is stated. The world does not force it: the purple ball can be carried to the key instead, which the third wrong plan does; the env pays that route too, so env_reward_matches is false. train: false keeps the card out of the 60-card set.
